tiers.name: descriptor node array
tiers.why: E23 watched only 0x548800/04/08. The head advanced 0x548800 = 0x548880 at boot-log line 10,168 and the SUCCESSOR node was unwatched -- E23 NAMED that as its residual. This covers the current node, the successor node, and two further nodes at the observed 0x80 stride.
tiers.guarantee: complete: every byte of four 128-byte nodes is inside a watched window

tiers.name: data region head
tiers.why: the 0xd48748 data pointer the descriptor published (bytes=0x13ac=5,036). A refill that rewrites from the start lands here first.

tiers.name: data region stride sample
tiers.why: the body of the 5,036 B. Full 8-byte cover would cost 630 entries and the per-store scan is linear in the watch count (diagWatchEmit), so the body is sampled instead of covered.
tiers.guarantee: any CONTIGUOUS run >= 121 B is caught (stride 128 - window 8 = 120 B max gap); an isolated write shorter than that inside the sampled span is NOT

tiers.name: data region tail
tiers.why: the last 128 B of the delivered region, where the final slice ended.

tiers.name: past-end extension
tiers.why: the 128 B immediately AFTER the 5,036 B. E24 measured that the feed ends with 15 zero bytes and no terminating start code, so a continuation would write exactly here.

tiers.name: staging buffer
tiers.why: E23 watched only the first 8 B of the buffer AddBs actually read its 5,040 B from. A refill of the staging buffer is the other way new bytes could appear.

tiers.name: kind-1 queue slot (+ chunk 0 header)
tiers.why: E27 named the kind-1 slot as ctx0->[0x24]+0 but had no guest address for it. E28 Mission 1 derives it: the STRM constructor sub_003E06D8 computes the slot array base and then the DATA REGION BASE from it, and E26 measured that data base in bytes (sceCdRead buf=0xd48740). Running the identity backwards over the allocator's 64-byte alignment floor (sub_00253AD0) gives ctx0=0xd48300 uniquely, so the kind-1 slot is 0xd486ec: owner +0, kind +4, bytes +8, head +0xC. This tier covers the whole window the slot array could occupy at ANY alignment, so the boot MEASURES the address. It is extended down to 0xd48740 so chunk 0's header -- E27's named blind spot, where sub_003E12E0 strips the tag in the same breath as it advances the head -- is visible.
tiers.guarantee: complete: every byte of [0xd486e0, 0xd48748) is inside a watched 8-byte window

p_meaning.p1: slot+8 (byte count) and slot+0xC (head) carry P1; both receive GUEST STORES (walker 0x3dffc0/0x3dffc4, dequeue 0x3e134c/0x3e13c8), so P1 is observable
p_meaning.control: slot+0 is written once at construction with ctx0 itself (0x3e0914), which independently confirms the address if it emits
p_meaning.chunk0_header: 0xd48740 magic / 0xd48744 tagged length -- E27 named 0xd48744 as outside every E24 tier, so chunk 0's own tag store was never observable

cost_model.caveat: a two-point fit on two runs, so the slope is indicative, not measured. It is used only to SIZE the list conservatively; the driver records the actual span-complete time so the next lane can refit.
cost_model.why_not_full_cover: full 8-byte cover of the 5,036 B body would be 630 entries; the same fit predicts span-complete at ~64 s, leaving ~11 s of post-park window instead of ~50 s.

e28_change.what: ONE tier appended; the 230-entry E26/E24 vector is carried verbatim and unreordered
e28_change.cost: E26 refit the model to k=0.00806 s/entry, base=7.683 s on three points, so 13 extra entries cost about 0.10 s of span-complete against a 75 s bound
